agree.reason: This wary backer is likely to warm to the open cost figures and the refusal to call an unprinted game a hit, but with no delivery date or fulfilment plan, a reader burned before may still hold back.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the brief, the per-copy and backers-needed numbers are correct, the request to call it a proven hit is turned down with 'No game is a hit before it's in a box', and the only additions are naming BoardGameGeek and saying 'three years'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $11.60 a copy and 572 backers, but it never adds printing plus shipping (about $22.5k against $28k) to show the budget holds, and never compares 572 with the 1,240-person list (about 46% need to back), which would help the case.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative plainly (the game stays a prototype on the designer's table), but it never sets the pace needed, 572 backers, against the support already shown by the 1,240 sign-ups.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition names a number and a consequence ($28,000 or the game stays a prototype), but it gives no campaign end date or delivery date the reader could check.

objections.reason: It names and meets the first-time-creator worry with the factory quote and shipping cost, but it leaves the questions this reader cares about open: cost overruns, platform fees, timeline, and what happens if the 1,500-copy run is underfunded.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured crowdfunding pitch of about 430 words, a little under the roughly 500 asked for.
